text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak President Michal Kovac warned that a thwarted referendum on NATO membership and direct presidential elections last May indicated that the ruling coalition may attempt to manipulate next year's general elections.
- Employees of the state-run bus transport company in Svidnik, eastern Slovakia, on Monday broke off their strike after agreeing with management on a salary increase.
- The government is expected to discuss an amendment to the banking law during its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda does not include any other major economic items.
- Operating revenues of VSZ Steel, the main producing unit of steel maker VSZ, totalled 18.96 billlion crowns in the first half of this year, some 492 million crowns more than originally planned.

- State-owned monopoly electricity producer, Slovenske Elektrarne, said it would invest some 1.5 billion crowns in 1997 into upgrading safety systems at its sole operating nuclear power plant at Jaslovske Bohunice.
- VSZ said it planned to produce some 300,000 tonnes of sheet steel for car production this year. VSZ's biggest customer is Czech car maker Skoda, which bought 110,000 tonnes of sheet steel in 1997.
- The government plans to reduce the amount of medical drugs wholesalers in Slovakia.

- Fiat Slovakia said it had no plans to increase its car prices despite a recently introduced seven-percent import surcharge. Fiat said it would only boost prices in the case of administrative moves such as crown devaluation.
- Alexander Rezes, one of VSZ's main owners and President of Czech soccer club Sparta Praha, said he expected Lothar Matthaus to sign a transfer to Sparta in the near future.
- Slovakia's largest commercial bank, VUB, said none of the companies which had chosen VUB to manage their corporate bond issues so far had any problems with repayment of the bonds.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski will begin a two-day official visit to Slovakia on August 20.
- Minister of Agriculture, Peter Baco, said Slovakia's grain harvest in 1997 will cover the country's entire annual consumption.
- Kim Woo-Chung, Chairman of the board of South Korea's Daewoo Corp. met with Finance and Economics Ministers Sergej Kozlik and Karol Cesnek to discuss possible business activities in Slovakia.
PRAVDA - The U.S. has asked Slovakia to destroy the SS-23 missiles on its territory.
- The Ministry of Agriculture estimates heavy rains and floods in July casued financial damage worth some 1.342 billion crowns to agricultural production.

- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) said in a reaction to Friday's meeting with his Hungarian counterpart Gyula Horn, that Budapest should create "similar conditions" for Slovakia's minority as Bratislava created for Hungarians in Slovakia.

SME - Deputy Chairman of the Opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), Ivan Simko, said the Meciar-Horn meeting brought no positive results and that Slovakia should be better prepared for future international meetings.
PRACA - HZDS still demands parliament approve the privatisation of the second terrestrial channel of the public Slovak Television (STV).
- The opposition Democratic Union (DU) said it had information that state-run monopoly gas distributor SPP is to finance a company expected to win the privatisation tender for STV's second channel.
-- Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
